Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for seeing Mr. Davis, a 34-year-old software analyst, for a specialist evaluation. He initially presented to my clinic for a routine checkup six months ago with no prior medical records. He is currently asymptomatic, takes no daily medications, does not use tobacco or alcohol, and has an unremarkable family history.

Physical examination today is completely normal. His blood pressure is 122/76 mmHg, heart sounds are regular without murmurs, the chest is clear to auscultation bilaterally, and there is no peripheral edema or rash.

Laboratory evaluations over the past several months reveal sustained impairment of his baseline renal function, first identified during his initial visit earlier this year. His serum creatinine has consistently hovered between 1.7 and 1.9 mg/dL, with an estimated filtration rate persistently reduced at approximately 46 mL/min/1.73 m2. Subsequent spot quantification demonstrated substantial protein spill in the urine, with a urine protein-to-creatinine ratio measured at 1.3 g/g. Reassuringly, his decline in excretory capacity is non-critical, and he shows no evidence of stage 5 renal failure. Renal ultrasonography performed last month showed symmetric, normal-sized kidneys with preserved corticomedullary differentiation and no obstruction.

Given the persistence of these renal lab abnormalities and urinary protein loss in an otherwise healthy young man, I would value your assessment regarding the appropriate diagnostic pathway and long-term management strategy.

Sincerely,
Dr. Arthur Pendelton
Oakridge Family Medicine
